RagShortTexts: Vienna guarded the Danube trade crossroads, disputed between Bohemia and Hungary.

Variants.Content: Perched on the southern bank of the Danube, Vienna served as the proud ducal seat of the Babenbergs. Anchored around Romanesque St. Stephen's Cathedral, its strategic position made it the fiercely contested prize between Ottokar II of Bohemia and Béla IV of Hungary following the extinction of the ducal line in 1246.

Vienna enforces mandatory staple rights (Stapelrecht); merchant barges transporting Alpine salt and Hungarian grain must unlade cargo for three days, enriching civic burghers and drawing sovereign suitors.
Heavy barges clog the Danube wharves with smoked beef and shields. Whichever army holds Vienna immediately throws chain barricades across the streets to regulate armed travelers.
